en.title: GTA 6 Boss's Past Includes Role in Iconic Christmas Hit
en.summary: Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of Rockstar Games, has a surprising connection to one of the most beloved holiday films of all time. Before leading the charge on Grand Theft Auto VI, Zelnick played a pivotal role in saving a Christmas classic from cancellation.
en.body:
When we think of **Strauss Zelnick**, our minds immediately go to **Grand Theft Auto VI**, the most anticipated game on the horizon. As the CEO of **Take-Two Interactive**, the company behind **Rockstar Games**, Zelnick is at the helm of one of the biggest entertainment franchises in history. However, Zelnick’s journey to the top of the gaming world is far more varied than many might expect, including a significant chapter in Hollywood history.

In 1990, a little film called **Home Alone** was in jeopardy. Warner Bros. had begun production on the Christmas comedy, but faced with budget concerns, they pulled the plug just four days in – a move Zelnick described as something that "never happens." At the time, Zelnick was the president and COO of 20th Century Fox, a relatively young executive at 32. He, along with chairman Joe Roth, saw the potential in the project and stepped in to provide the necessary funding for director **Christopher Columbus** and writer **John Hughes**. This gamble paid off handsomely, as **Home Alone** became a global phenomenon, grossing over $476 million worldwide against a modest $13 million budget and earning two Oscar nominations. The film also launched the career of **Macaulay Culkin**, solidifying his role as Kevin McCallister in popular culture.

## A Pivotal Career Shift

Despite his success in film, Zelnick's sights were set on a different frontier. He recognized the burgeoning potential of interactive entertainment. In 1993, he made a bold decision to leave his high-profile position in Hollywood. He voluntarily left Fox, taking a significant pay cut to move to Silicon Valley and join a small video game company called **Crystal Dynamics** as its president and CEO. This move demonstrated a clear foresight into the future of entertainment, prioritizing the growing interactive space over the established film industry.

## What This Means for Gamers

This revelation adds a fascinating layer to Zelnick’s leadership. It suggests a business acumen honed across different entertainment sectors, a deep understanding of what makes a story resonate with a broad audience, and a willingness to take calculated risks. For fans eagerly awaiting **GTA 6**, knowing that the executive guiding its release has a proven track record of identifying and nurturing massive hits, even in seemingly unrelated fields, can only fuel anticipation. It hints at a leadership that values creative vision and understands the long game required to build enduring franchises.

## What's Next

While **GTA 6** is slated for release in November 2026, Zelnick's past success in both film and games underscores the potential for **Take-Two Interactive** to deliver a truly monumental experience. Details regarding the game's final marketing push and any potential tie-ins remain under wraps, but this historical context provides an intriguing backdrop.

content_raw: One of the most memorable and beloved Christmas movies is 1990's Home Alone, but it almost didn't happen, and the head of GTA 6 's parent company played a role in bringing the movie to market. Strauss Zelnick, the current CEO of Rockstar Games owner Take-Two, was the president and COO of 20th Century Fox at the time--he was among the youngest-ever Hollywood CEOs at the age of 32. Warner Bros. was originally backing Home Alone and had actually begun production on the movie until budget concerns prompted the studio to pull the plug. "Four days into production, they shut down the picture and canceled it. That never happens," Zelnick told David Rubenstein . Fox, under the leadership of chairman Joe Roth and Zelnick as president, swooped in and gave the filmmakers--including director Christopher Columbus and writer John Hughes--the money to make Home Alone. That turned out to be a fantastic investment for Fox, as Home Alone ranked as one of the top five highest-grossing movies of the year in the US. It grossed more than $476 million globally against a $13 million budget, and it picked up two Oscar nominations. Home Alone also helped launch the career of Macaulay Culkin, and his role of Kevin remains his most memorable part. So why didn't Zelnick keep making movies? Zelnick was on top of the world as a film executive after Home Alone. However, he said he saw a bright future in the interactive entertainment business, so he left Fox in 1993 to join Crystal Dynamics where he served as president and CEO. "I left Fox voluntarily, which no one ever does, to move to Silicon Valley, take a 95% pay cut and become the pre-revenue CEO of a little tiny video game company called Crystal Dynamics in 1993," he said in the Rubenstein interview. After Crystal Dynamics, Zelnick shifted to the music business in the role of CEO as BMG Entertainment from 1994 to 2000. During that time, BMG started a gaming unit, BMG Interactive, which published the original GTA in 1997 . After that, Zelnick and an investor group took over Take-Two, which was in a tough financial spot at the time and was sued by the US government for accounting fraud. Since the takeover, Take-Two has thrived. Its share price exploded from about $10 in 2007 to more than $220 today, and Take-Two today has a market cap of over $40 billion. The GTA franchise is a juggernaut at Take-Two, but it actually only accounts for 15% of the company's revenue in a non-release quarter . Take-Two today owns and operates a number of big non-GTA franchises, including NBA 2K, Borderlands, Mafia, BioShock, Civilization, and more. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It's reportedly already sold close to 15 million copies and generated nearly $1.5 billion in revenue.
